newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares slip as consolidation continues.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares slip as consolidation continues.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.9 percent on Thursday on profit-taking after recent rapid gains but traders see market rebounding as selling pressure is showing signs of subsiding.
"Most shares on the market are following moves in Lek's shares. I think Lek cannot fall much lower, so if not tomorrow -- growth will resume next week," Andrej Kavcic of brokerage Ilirika said.
The 10-share SBI index fell 13.87 points to 1,520, marking the second day of losses after a 13 day winning streak.
Turnover rose to 429.8 million tolars from 413.7 million tolars. Overall 13 shares fell, two rose and three were unchanged, while seven were untraded.
Drug maker Lek's A issue was the most active, falling 2.23 percent to 29,000 tolars on volume of 6,041 shares for total turnover of 179.3 million tolars.
Health resort operator Terme Catez led the day's decliners, falling 6.67 percent to 14,000 tolars on volume of 1,702 shares for total turnover of 24.9 million tolars.
Warehouse company BTC was the biggest gainer, jumping 6.92 percent to 13,900 tolars on volume of 845 shares.
